description: Enhance the Workflow section: reduce vertical whitespace, scatter nodes organically, enrich steps with description + stat, add progressive reveal animation with pulse/glow that loops, and lock down the canvas as fully read-only.

userStories.title: Make canvas fully read-only and remove background grid
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the React Flow canvas to be completely non-interactive so users cannot accidentally drag, zoom, select, or draw on it.
acceptanceCriteria: Add nodesConnectable={false} prop to ReactFlow to prevent edge drawing
Add elementsSelectable={false} prop to ReactFlow to prevent node/edge selection
Keep existing read-only props: panOnDrag={false}, zoomOnScroll={false}, nodesDraggable={false}, zoomOnPinch={false}, preventScrolling={false}
Remove the <Background> component from inside ReactFlow (no more grid dots)
In WorkflowNode.tsx, remove 'hover:shadow-md transition-shadow' from the outer div class (no hover feedback)
Add CSS override to set cursor to 'default' on the React Flow canvas container (override the default grab cursor). Use a wrapper div with style or a className targeting .react-flow
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en, try to drag/zoom/click nodes in workflow section — nothing interactive should happen

userStories.title: Reduce section vertical footprint
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the workflow section to be more compact so it doesn't dominate the page with excessive whitespace.
acceptanceCriteria: In Workflow.tsx, change section padding from 'py-20 md:py-28 lg:py-32' to 'py-12 md:py-16 lg:py-20'
Change header margin-bottom from 'mb-12 md:mb-20' to 'mb-8 md:mb-12'
Change tab navigation margin-bottom from 'mb-10 md:mb-14' to 'mb-6 md:mb-10'
Canvas height stays at h-[280px] for now (will be adjusted in US-003 for scattered layout)
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en and confirm the workflow section is visually more compact with less whitespace above and below

userStories.title: Organic scattered node layout
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the workflow nodes to feel organically placed like a mind map rather than sitting on a rigid alternating grid.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the uniform stepsToNodes position calculation (currently index * 200 for x, alternating 0/140 for y) with a scattered layout using predefined position offsets
Use a positions array like: [{x:0,y:60}, {x:220,y:0}, {x:410,y:100}, {x:640,y:20}, {x:830,y:110}, {x:1040,y:40}] — no two adjacent nodes at the same height, varied horizontal gaps
For workflows with fewer or more than 6 steps, generate positions dynamically with random-looking but deterministic offsets (e.g. using index-based math, not Math.random)
Change default edge type to 'smoothstep' or 'bezier' in defaultEdgeOptions so edges curve nicely between scattered positions
Increase canvas height from h-[280px] to h-[340px] to accommodate vertical scatter range
Left-to-right reading order is maintained (step 1 leftmost, last step rightmost)
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en and confirm workflow nodes appear scattered/organic on desktop — not in a rigid grid pattern
userStories.notes: The scattered positions should feel intentional and curated, not chaotic. Think mind-map positioning.

userStories.title: Extend step interface and update node components for description and stat
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the WorkflowStep interface and node components to support rendering a description and stat alongside the existing label.
acceptanceCriteria: Add optional 'description' (string) and 'stat' (string) fields to the WorkflowStep interface in Workflow.tsx
Add 'description' and 'stat' to WorkflowNodeData interface in WorkflowNode.tsx
Update stepsToNodes function to pass description and stat through to node data
Update WorkflowNode component: render description below the label in smaller text (text-xs text-forest-600, max 1 line, truncated if needed)
Update WorkflowNode component: render stat as a small coral-colored accent (e.g. text-xs text-coral-600 font-semibold, or a small chip/badge)
Increase node min-width from min-w-[140px] to min-w-[200px] to accommodate new content
Update MobileWorkflowStep component to also display description and stat (description below label, stat as small accent text)
Both description and stat are optional — component renders without them gracefully (backward compatible)
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en and confirm nodes still render correctly (they won't show description/stat yet since dictionaries haven't been updated)
userStories.notes: Keep the node compact despite new content. Description should be one short line. Stat should be very small, like a data point badge.

userStories.title: Add description and stat content to all workflow dictionary entries
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want each workflow step to show a short description and a relevant stat so I better understand what each step involves.
acceptanceCriteria: Update workflow.workflows[] steps in da.json, en.json, de.json — add 'description' and 'stat' to each step in all 3 workflows (club-onboarding, order-lifecycle, agreement-management)
Update audienceWorkflows[] steps in da.json, en.json, de.json — add 'description' and 'stat' to each step in all 3 workflows (brand-admin, club-admin, coach-staff)
Update sportsPage.workflow.steps in da.json, en.json, de.json — add 'description' and 'stat' to all 4 steps
Descriptions should be one short sentence explaining what happens at this step (e.g. 'Set up your club profile and team structure')
Stats should be short punchy metrics or data points (e.g. '~2 min', '100% digital', 'Real-time', '1-click')
All 3 languages have complete translations — no empty strings
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en and confirm workflow nodes now display their description and stat text
userStories.notes: This is a content-heavy story. Stats should feel credible and useful — things like time estimates, automation %, or capability keywords. Use placeholder-quality content that reads well.

userStories.title: Progressive reveal animation triggered by scroll
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the workflow to animate into view when I scroll to it — nodes appearing one by one with edges drawing in and a pulse on the active node — so the section feels alive.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an Intersection Observer (useEffect + IntersectionObserver API) that detects when the workflow section enters the viewport (threshold ~0.3)
When section enters viewport: all React Flow nodes and edges start invisible (opacity 0, scale 0.8 via CSS)
Nodes reveal one at a time: fade-in + scale to 1.0 transition (~400ms per node, ~300ms delay between nodes)
After each node fully appears, the edge from the previous node draws in (use CSS stroke-dasharray/stroke-dashoffset animation on the SVG path, ~300ms)
The currently-revealing node has a coral pulse/glow effect: a box-shadow animation (0 0 0 4px rgba(249,123,95,0.4)) that pulses 2-3 times then fades when the next node starts revealing
Animation state managed via useRef for timers and useState for current visible step index
All timers cleaned up on unmount (return cleanup in useEffect)
Tab switching (when activeWorkflow changes) resets animation to step 0 and replays
Animation is desktop-only — mobile renders all steps immediately with no animation
Typecheck passes
Visual verification: Navigate to /en, scroll down to workflow section, confirm nodes animate in one by one with edges drawing between them
userStories.notes: CSS approach: add a wrapper className to each node that toggles between 'workflow-node-hidden' (opacity:0, transform:scale(0.8)) and 'workflow-node-visible' (opacity:1, transform:scale(1), transition:all 400ms). For edges, use custom CSS on .react-flow__edge-path to animate stroke-dashoffset. The pulse can be a CSS @keyframes animation applied via a 'workflow-node-active' class.

userStories.title: Animation loop with pause and reset
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want the animation to loop — pausing after the last step, then resetting and replaying — so the section always has motion.
acceptanceCriteria: After the last node and its incoming edge finish animating, hold the completed state for 2.5 seconds
After the pause, all nodes and edges fade out together (~300ms transition to opacity 0)
After fade-out completes, restart the animation from step 1
Loop continues indefinitely while the section is in the viewport
When the section scrolls out of view (Intersection Observer disconnect), pause all timers and stop the animation
When the section scrolls back into view, reset to step 0 and begin the animation fresh from the start
Tab switching clears all timers and restarts animation for the new workflow
No memory leaks — all setInterval/setTimeout refs cleaned up on unmount and on every reset
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: The animation lifecycle: reveal nodes one by one → hold complete state 2.5s → fade all out 300ms → pause 200ms → restart. Use a single orchestrating useEffect that manages the full cycle via setTimeout chains or a step-based state machine.
